primary_transformation: Antenna pigment absorption and Forster energy transfer to PSII/PSI reaction centers
measurable_output: Absorbed photon fraction (absorptance) and energy transfer efficiency
D_parameters: Absorption spectrum constraints; pigment stoichiometry (Chl a/b ~3:1); antenna size (~200-300 Chl per PSII); LHCII trimer geometry; energy funneling gradient
C_parameters: Excitation energy delivered to P680 and P700; antenna state transitions (State 1/2); non-photochemical quenching activation threshold
notes: Absorptance of green leaves ~0.85 of PAR. Energy transfer efficiency within LHCII >95%. Quantum yield of absorbed-to-excited state ~0.90. Reference: Blankenship 2014 Molecular Mechanisms of Photosynthesis.

physical_state_in: Excitation energy at P680; H2O as electron donor
physical_state_out: Plastoquinol (PQH2); O2 released; protons into lumen
primary_transformation: Water oxidation at Mn4CaO5 cluster; charge separation at P680; plastoquinone reduction
measurable_output: O2 evolution rate; quantum yield of PSII (Fv/Fm)
D_parameters: Excitation threshold ~1.82 eV; Mn4CaO5 cluster stoichiometry; QB binding site specificity; tyrosine Z intermediate; pH gradient requirement; D1 protein turnover under high light
C_parameters: O2 evolution (4e- per O2); 2 PQH2 per 4 photons; 4 H+ released into lumen per 2 H2O split; feeds electron transport chain
notes: Maximum O2 evolution ~25-35 µmol O2 m-2 s-1 in saturating light (spinach). Fv/Fm (max quantum yield PSII) = 0.83 dark-adapted. Reference: Maxwell & Johnson 2000 J Exp Bot.

physical_state_out: Reduced plastocyanin (PC); proton gradient across thylakoid membrane
primary_transformation: Plastoquinol oxidation at cytochrome b6f; Rieske iron-sulfur cluster; plastocyanin reduction; proton pumping (Q-cycle)
measurable_output: Electron transfer rate; proton motive force (pmf)
D_parameters: PQ pool size (~7-15 PQ per PSII); cytochrome b6f rate limitation ~100-200 s-1; pmf threshold for ATP synthase activation; pH gating (low lumenal pH slows cytochrome b6f); antenna state transitions regulated by PQ redox state
C_parameters: Plastocyanin reduction (feeds PSI); 2 H+ pumped per electron via Q-cycle (total ~4 H+ per 2 electrons passed); thylakoid membrane energization; state transition signals
notes: Rate-limiting step of the linear electron flow chain under most conditions. Cytochrome b6f turnover ~100-200 s-1 at 25°C. pmf ~150-200 mV under steady-state illumination. Reference: Cramer et al. 2011 Biochim Biophys Acta.

primary_transformation: Second photochemical reaction; P700 excitation at ~1.77 eV; ferredoxin-NADP+ reductase (FNR) catalysis
measurable_output: NADPH production rate; PSI quantum yield
D_parameters: P700 excitation threshold ~1.77 eV; ferredoxin specificity; NADP+ availability (limits when Calvin cycle slow); FNR binding; cyclic vs linear electron flow balance; iron-sulfur cluster geometry (Fx Fa Fb)
C_parameters: Reduced ferredoxin (feeds FNR and other reductases); NADPH synthesis at ~1 per 2 electrons; cyclic electron flow option (feeds proton gradient without net NADPH); nitrite reduction; sulfite reduction side reactions
notes: PSI quantum yield (Y(I)) ~0.75-0.85 under moderate light. NADPH production ~8-12 µmol m-2 s-1 in steady-state C3 leaf. Reference: Klughammer & Schreiber 1994 Planta.

physical_state_in: Proton motive force (pmf) across thylakoid membrane
primary_transformation: Rotary chemiosmotic phosphorylation; c-ring rotation driven by H+ flux; gamma subunit rotation drives ADP phosphorylation
D_parameters: pmf threshold ~3-4 H+ per ATP synthesized (c14/CF1CF0 in spinach); ΔpH component dominance (~70%); Δψ component (~30%); ADP and Pi availability; CF1 regulatory subunit (thioredoxin-mediated light activation)
C_parameters: ATP synthesis (3 ATP per ~3-4 H+); thylakoid membrane discharge; stroma alkalinization (pH rises ~0.5 during illumination); regulatory coupling to Calvin cycle demand
notes: ATP/NADPH ratio produced by linear electron flow ~1.28 (H+/ATP = 14/3 = 4.67 in spinach). Actual demand for C3 cycle = 1.5 ATP/NADPH. Cyclic flow supplements ATP. Reference: Allen 2003 Science.

primary_transformation: CO2 fixation by RuBisCO (Rubisco); competitive oxygenation reaction (photorespiration); RuBP carboxylase/oxygenase chemistry
measurable_output: Net CO2 assimilation rate (An); Rubisco carboxylation rate (Vc)
D_parameters: CO2 Km ~9-10 µM (chloroplast); O2 competition (Kc/Ko specificity factor Sc/o ~80 mol/mol at 25°C); RuBP regeneration capacity; Rubisco activation state (~60-90%); Mg2+ and CO2 requirement for activation; stomatal conductance (CO2 diffusion limit)
C_parameters: CO2 fixed as 3-PGA; but ~25% of CO2 is lost via photorespiration under current atmosphere (21% O2); 2-phosphoglycolate recycled through photorespiratory pathway at energy cost; net carbon gain per unit light absorbed
notes: Net CO2 assimilation An = 15-25 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1 (sunlit C3 leaf at 380 ppm CO2 25°C). Rubisco oxygenation/carboxylation ratio Vo/Vc ~0.25 at 25°C 21% O2. Reference: Farquhar et al. 1980 Planta.

physical_state_in: 3-PGA; ATP and NADPH from light reactions
primary_transformation: ATP-dependent phosphorylation of 3-PGA; NADPH-dependent reduction to G3P; phosphoribulokinase (PRK) regenerates RuBP
measurable_output: G3P production rate; ATP and NADPH consumption per CO2 fixed
D_parameters: ATP stoichiometry (3 ATP per CO2 in linear flow); NADPH stoichiometry (2 NADPH per CO2); PRK specificity for RuBP; phosphate translocator (TPT) capacity; GAPDH (NADPH-dependent) specificity; regulatory thioredoxin control of PRK and GAPDH
C_parameters: G3P export to cytosol for sucrose synthesis; RuBP regenerated (5 G3P consumed per 3 CO2 fixed); starch synthesis signal (excess G3P); Pi recycled back to stroma
notes: Stoichiometry well defined: 3 ATP + 2 NADPH consumed per CO2 fixed into G3P. G3P production tracks An directly. Reference: Raines 2003 Photosynth Res.

physical_state_in: G3P (triose phosphate) in stroma; ADP-glucose for starch
physical_state_out: Sucrose in cytosol; starch granules in chloroplast; phloem-loaded sucrose
primary_transformation: Triose phosphate export via plastid phosphate translocator (TPT); cytosolic sucrose synthesis (SPS); chloroplastic starch synthesis (AGPase); phloem loading
measurable_output: Net carbon export rate; sucrose:starch partitioning ratio
D_parameters: TPT transporter capacity and Pi availability; cytosolic Pi:triose-P ratio governs starch/sucrose balance; AGPase allosteric regulation (3-PGA activation; Pi inhibition); SPS phosphorylation state; sucrose feedback on phloem loading; night/day carbon remobilization cycles
C_parameters: Sucrose synthesis and export to phloem; starch synthesis and nocturnal remobilization; carbon allocated to growth and respiration; regulation of source-sink balance; feedback on upstream photosynthesis rate
notes: Sucrose synthesis rate estimated from starch+sucrose accumulation ~10-20 µmol C m-2 s-1 in illuminated spinach leaf. TPT flux ~3-5 µmol triose-P m-2 s-1. Export regulation partially opaque at phloem loading step. Reference: Stitt et al. 2010 Plant Cell Environ.
